provision_decisions.note: 6-1990/s37 charges stamp duty at the prescribed rate on every instrument relating to a transfer of immovable property in the Western Province. Excerpt verbatim. The corpus text transposes the words of paragraph (a) as OCR damage; the reading relied on is the only sensible one.
The definition of Transfer in 6-1990/s106 expressly includes a gift and excludes a deed of partition and an agreement to transfer; neither exclusion touches this deed.
6-1990/s48(1) verbatim. Subsections (2) and (3) of the same section are consistent with the map, and (3) covers the reserved gift that the enrichment expressly excludes.
Verbatim. The corpus has lost the (i) marker of the first limb of paragraph (c) through OCR; 43-1982/s71(c)(i) carries the same limb cleanly, so the limb structure is not in doubt.
The second limb and the whichever price is the lower instruction are both verbatim in 6-1990/s106.
43-1982/s71 paragraph (c) is verbatim and word for word the parallel of the provincial definition, including the requirement that improvements be made before the date of the gift instrument.

Excerpt verbatim but the role is overstated: 12-2006/s13 displaces the 1982 Act only so far as it is inconsistent with the 2006 Act, and the 2006 Act prescribes no valuation rule for gifted land, so 43-1982/s71 survives on that ground as much as on the parenthetical carve-out. Kept as supporting; it is not the charging route for land in the Western Province.
6-1990/s78(2) verbatim, and s78(1) says what the why_relevant field says it says.
6-1990/s51(a) verbatim: duty on an instrument of transfer is payable by the grantee except where there is an agreement to the contrary.

6-1990/s40(1) verbatim. Subsection (2) additionally allows payment to a prescribed bank against a certificate of payment, which is the usual route for a transfer of immovable property; the map does not rely on it.

Excerpt verbatim but it quotes only item (1) of the exemption list, so it does not on its face support a negative proposition. The verifier read the whole of 6-1990/s39: the list runs to six heads, all of them Government, foreign government, court document or testamentary, and none exempts a gift between family members.
43-1982/s15 verbatim, including subsection (3) on gifts subject to a reservation.
Added by the verifier. Definition of conveyance in 6-1990/s106, checked verbatim.

added_provisions.reason: The map moved from the charging section, which bites on an instrument relating to a transfer, straight to s.48(1), which fixes the base only where property is conveyed by an instrument. Nothing cited bridged transfer and conveyed. The definition of conveyance in 6-1990/s106 (includes conveyance on sale and every instrument by which property, or any interest in any property is transferred) closes that step, so it is added as indispensable to both questions with a defines edge to PROV-M047-003, and cited alongside it in the claim that states the base of the charge. The same interpretation section also defines gift as a transfer made voluntarily and without consideration in money or money's worth, and defines instrument to include every document relating to a transfer of immovable property in the Western Province; both are consistent with the map and were not added, to keep the added set to what the chain actually needs.

question_decisions.note: The chain holds on the corpus text: s.37 charges the instrument, s.106 defines Transfer to include a gift, s.106 defines conveyance so that s.48(1) reaches the deed, s.48(1) puts the duty on the value of the property conveyed, and paragraph (c) of the definition of value gives the lower of the acquisition-date open market price increased by later improvements and the open market price at the date of the deed. December 1977 is after 31 March 1977, so paragraph (c) and not paragraph (b) applies, and Rs.250,000 plus Rs.800,000 is Rs.1,050,000, lower than Rs.6,500,000. Paragraph selection and arithmetic are both correct. Hop count raised from four to five for the added definitional step. One rule claim about the 1982 Act is marked disputed; it is not load bearing for the conclusion.

The block is right. The verifier searched the corpus independently: 6-1990/s37 and 43-1982/s2 both say only at the prescribed rate, 12-2006/s3 leaves the rate to a Ministerial Order in the Gazette, and no rate Order, regulation or schedule is in the corpus. The base, the person liable and the time of payment are established, but no figure of duty can be produced. The requirement stays statute_only because the missing authority is subordinate legislation, not case law.

disagreements.researcher_position: 12-2006/s13 explains why the 1982 Act still speaks to this instrument, because instruments relating to the transfer of immovable property are carved out of the displacement of the 1982 Act.
disagreements.verifier_position: The carve-out is one route and not the cleanest. Section 13 displaces the 1982 Act only so far as it is inconsistent with the 2006 Act, and the 2006 Act prescribes no valuation rule for gifted immovable property, so there is no inconsistency for s.71 to yield to. Either way 43-1982/s71 is a parallel formulation and not the operative charge, which is provincial.

disagreements.researcher_position: Four hops: charge, Transfer includes gift, duty calculated on value, definition of value.
disagreements.verifier_position: Five. Section 48(1) is keyed to property conveyed, not to a transfer, so the definition of conveyance in s.106 is a further necessary definitional step on the researcher's own convention, under which the Transfer definition was itself counted as a hop.

unsupported_claims: CL-M047-Q01-005 marked disputed. It asserts that the 1982 Act's valuation rules continue to speak to instruments relating to the transfer of immovable property because those instruments are excepted from the displacement of that Act. The parenthetical in 12-2006/s13 is grammatically attached to the provisions relating to the Imposition of Stamp Duty, and the sentence goes on to displace Exemptions and any other provision only so far as inconsistent. The conclusion survives, but not for the stated reason, and the claim is not indispensable to the Rs.1,050,000 figure, which rests on the provincial statute alone.

CL-M047-Q01-006 and its provision PROV-M047-011 rest on the absence of an exemption while the recorded excerpt shows only the bail bond head. Checked against the full text of 6-1990/s39; the claim is sound but its recorded support was thin.
temporal_issues: Every provision relied on comes from a 1990 provincial statute applied to an October 2022 instrument. The corpus section records carry in_force_from_year 1990 and no latest_change_year, and no amendment to the Western Province Financial Statute is indexed. That is an absence of amendment tracking, not evidence that ss.37, 39, 40, 48, 51, 78 and 106 stood unamended in 2022. The map's temporal notes are accurate as far as they go, but a lawyer must confirm the 2022 text before this is treated as gold.

Paragraph (c) of the definition of value is pegged to 31 March 1977, a date contemporaneous with the 1982 national Act. Whether the provincial definition was rewritten between 1990 and 2022 cannot be established from these sources.
missing_definitions_or_exceptions: The definition of conveyance in 6-1990/s106 was missing and has been added as PROV-M047-901. Without it s.48(1), keyed to property conveyed, does not visibly reach a Deed of Gift.
6-1990/s106 also defines gift and instrument in terms that support the map; both were unremarked by the researcher and neither disturbs the result.

6-1990/s48(3), which values a gift subject to a reservation as if made without it, sits in a section already cited. The enrichment expressly makes this an outright gift, so it does not bite, but the pairing is worth a lawyer's eye.

1-1907/s31, rules to be observed by notaries, requires a notary not to attest a deed unless he has an assurance that the required stamp duty is provided. It reinforces the notarial duty in 6-1990/s78 and was not cited. Not indispensable, so not added.
case_law_dependence: None found. Both answers turn on charge, definition, base and rate, all statutory. The one soft edge is the Assessor's opinion of open market price, which is an administrative valuation question rather than a matter of judicial gloss.
enrichment_issues: FACT-M047-Q01-002 and FACT-M047-Q02-002 place the land at Maharagama in the Western Province. This is the enrichment choosing the governing enactment rather than filling a gap in the facts, and it is decisive: stamp duty on the transfer of immovable property is a provincial charge and the corpus holds only the Western Province statute. It is honestly labelled synthetic_decisive with a stated reason, but the whole answer sits on it.

FACT-M047-Q01-003 states that the Rs.250,000 paid in December 1977 was the open market price on that date. The statute makes the first limb the open market price in the opinion of the Assessor, not the price paid, so this fact substitutes for an assessor's opinion rather than supplying a fact from the world. It is needed to make the limb computable and is labelled decisive, but a lawyer should say whether a gold answer may assume it.
FACT-M047-Q01-004 dates the improvements to 1996 to 1999. Necessary, since the first limb admits only improvements made after acquisition and before the deed, and the paper gives no date.

No statute name, section number or figure of duty appears in either enriched background, and neither states the Rs.1,050,000 conclusion. Naming the Western Province does narrow the field of applicable law, which is inherent in that fact being decisive.
duplicate_or_leak_issues: M047-Q01 and M047-Q02 carry identical enriched backgrounds and five facts each with the same wording under different fact ids. That is proper for two items on one matter background, but a scorer treating the enriched backgrounds as independent scenarios would double count them.

The Q02 gold answer states the base as Rs.1,050,000, which is the whole answer to Q01. If the two questions are presented separately in that order, Q02's rule and application sections leak Q01's conclusion.

lawyer_questions: Is it acceptable for a benchmark gold answer to fix the province by enrichment? The paper names no location, stamp duty on the transfer of immovable property is levied province by province, and the corpus holds only the Western Province Financial Statute. If the answer is no, M047-Q01 becomes blocked for scenario ambiguity along with M047-Q02.

Did ss.37, 39, 40, 48, 51, 78 and 106 of the Western Province Financial Statute stand in the corpus wording in October 2022? No amendment to that Statute is indexed here, so the temporal position is asserted from silence.

May the first limb of paragraph (c) be satisfied by the price the donor actually paid, on a stated fact that the 1977 purchase was at arm's length, when the statute makes the limb the open market price in the opinion of the Assessor?
Should the definition of conveyance in s.106 count as a separate reasoning hop, as the verifier has recorded, or be folded into the step it serves?

What was the prescribed rate for a deed of gift of immovable property in the Western Province in October 2022, and where is the instrument that prescribes it? Supplying it would unblock M047-Q02 outright, since the base is settled at Rs.1,050,000.
